لَصَصٌ Nearness together of the أَضْرَاس [or teeth, or molar teeth, or all the teeth except the central incisors,] (S, M, A, K,) so that no interstice is seen between them; (M;) as also رَصَصٌ. (M, art. رص.) ―
-b2- And Nearness together of two legs of a quadruped, and of the two thighs: and nearness together of the upper parts of the two knees: (M:) or nearness together of the two shoulder-joints, (K,) or of the upper parts thereof, so that they nearly touch the ears: (M:) or nearness together of the two shoulder-blades: (M:) and a contraction of the elbows of the horse towards his [breast, or that part of it which is called the] زَوْر; (K;) and their cleaving to that part; which is a quality approved in a horse. (TA.) ―
-b3- Also, Nearness of the forehead to the eyebrow. (IKtt, TA.) ＝
-A2- See also لُصُوصِيَّةٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
